items.title: Stock Radar: Sona BLW stock breaks out from 11-month consolidation to hit fresh 52-week high; time to buy?
items.description: Sona BLW Precision Forgings stock has broken out from an 11-month consolidation. This move pushed the stock to a fresh 52-week high. Experts suggest buying the stock for a target of Rs 661 in the next 1-2 months. The stock shows strong momentum indicators, indicating a positive trend shift and potential for further upside.

items.title: Tata Elxsi shares in focus as Q4 net profit jumps 28%, revenue up 9% to Rs 994 crore
items.description: Tata Elxsi reported a strong Q4FY26 performance with a sharp rise in net profit and steady revenue growth. Margins remained healthy, supported by deal wins and segmental strength in media and transportation. Sequential improvement was robust, reflecting improving momentum and continued traction across key verticals and strategic business segments.

items.title: LIC Housing Finance among 5 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On April 21, in the Nifty200 segment, five stocks appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Karur Vysya Bank among 5 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: Five stocks from the Nifty500 segment that gained over 3% were identified using the RSI Trending Up scan on April 21, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is rising, suggesting strengthening price momentum in the stock. This may signal potential upward movement and can be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: ICICI Bank, Mastek among 5 stocks that could give 10-30% return
items.description: Brokerages continue to highlight selective opportunities across financials, housing finance, IT, pharma services, and new-age fintech plays, with most maintaining a constructive stance on earnings visibility and growth momentum.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 14 stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on April 21, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator to determine the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Trent set to announce its first-ever bonus issue today: What Zudio-parent's 5 lakh shareholders should know
items.description: Trent (Zudio parent) is set to consider its first-ever bonus issue today, making it a key trigger for its nearly 5 lakh shareholders.

items.title: GIFT Nifty hints at a gap-down start. Should investors brace for another weak session?
items.description: Indian markets experienced a strong session on Tuesday, with the Nifty rising nearly 1% driven by positive global sentiment, robust Q4 earnings, and easing crude prices. Volatility also saw a significant pullback. Investors are now keenly watching the second round of US-Iran talks, with hopes for progress despite elevated tensions.

items.title: Stocks in news: SBI Life, Trent, Tata Investment, HCL Tech, Suzlon Energy
items.description: In today's trade, shares of SBI Life, Trent, Tata Investment, HCL Tech, Suzlon Energy among others will be in focus due to various news developments.

items.title: It's not just war that brought rupee down, it needs better support
items.description: The West Asia conflict has accelerated INR depreciation, necessitating a rethink of India's economic fundamentals. Short-term measures include raising domestic interest rates and equalizing onshore tax regulations for asset classes. Longer-term, building world-class universities, encouraging local tourism, and potentially redesigning the INR symbol are proposed to foster resilience and economic growth.

items.title: DSP MF sees attractive entry point in large private banks
items.description: “Without pencilling in any re-rating, large private banks present an attractive opportunity for investors today,” said DSP in a note.  “More price decline will make them more attractive.”

items.title: As FPIs continue to sell, outflows likely to rise before inflows revive
items.description: "The financial services sector has the biggest weight on benchmark Nifty; so when there is broad-based selling, banking and financial services' share in foreign selling tends to be higher," said U R Bhat, co-founder & director, Alphaniti.

items.title: Fairfax likely to buy 10% more in IIFL Capital via preferential allotment
items.description: Fairfax Financial Holdings plans to boost its stake in IIFL Capital Services. The deal is valued at approximately ₹1,000 crore. This move will see Fairfax's holding increase by about 10%. The transaction is expected to trigger an open offer under Indian regulations. Prem Watsa's firm is doubling down on its investment after thorough due diligence.

items.title: D-Street bounces as traders cover short bets ahead of peace talks
items.description: Indian markets saw significant gains on Tuesday, with the Nifty and Sensex rising over 0.9% and 1% respectively. This surge was driven by traders cutting bearish bets ahead of US-Iran peace talks and a moderation in foreign institutional selling. Technical indicators suggest a bullish outlook, with the Nifty potentially moving towards 24,800-25,000.

items.title: Life insurers log 16% premium growth in FY26 on GST relief, shift to high-margin products
items.description: India’s life insurance industry recorded a 16% rise in new business premiums to ₹4.59 lakh crore in FY26, driven by GST exemption benefits, stronger demand for regular premium policies, and a strategic shift towards higher-margin protection and long-term savings products.

items.title: HCL Tech shares wipe out Rs 38,000 crore as target price falls to Rs 1,165. Why every second broker is busy downgrading
items.description: HCL Technologies shares plummeted nearly 10%, wiping out Rs 38,000 crore in market cap following a brutal Q4 earnings report. The IT major missed revenue, margin, and guidance targets, triggering widespread broker downgrades and price target cuts. Analysts are scrambling to reprice the stock amid concerns over client-specific headwinds and AI-driven deflation.

items.title: Vijay Kedia buys 44 lakh shares of this smallcap company in March, stock rallies 9% today. Do you own?
items.description: Websol Energy Systems shares surged after investor Vijay Kedia emerged in its latest shareholding data with over 1% stake. The development boosted sentiment, driving strong short-term gains. The company also plans to consider a dividend, while long-term stock performance remains volatile despite significant multiyear returns in recent years.

items.title: BHEL among 6 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open Interest
items.description: As of April 21, there was a notable surge in futures open interest for six stocks in the NSE F&O pack, contributing to a total increase in open interest of over 6% as compared to the previous trade. A significant uptick in futures open interest signifies a substantial growth in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a specific security. This uptrend reflects an increasing number of participants either initiating new positions or expanding the size of their existing positions within the futures market.

items.title: How Ashish Kacholia, Mukul Agrawal, Madhu Kela, Dolly Khanna reshuffled portfolios amid Iran war?
items.description: Amid a sharp market sell-off triggered by Iran war tensions and rising oil prices, marquee investors like Ashish Kacholia, Mukul Agrawal, Madhusudan Kela, and Dolly Khanna actively reshuffled portfolios, cutting risks while selectively adding stocks, signalling a strategic response to volatility and long-term opportunity creation.

items.title: Smallcap stock Rolex Rings share price rockets 26% in two days ahead of board meet to consider buyback
items.description: Rolex Rings shares surged nearly 9% as the company's board is set to consider its first-ever share buyback on April 23. The stock has seen a significant 35% rise in just six sessions, fueled by the buyback announcement and strong Q3 financial results. The company reported a 136% jump in net profit and improved EBITDA margins.

items.title: Tata Power vs Adani Power: As temperatures soar, which stock will shine?
items.description: Shares of Tata Power and Adani Power surged as heatwave alerts from the India Meteorological Department raised expectations of higher electricity demand, with analysts weighing their risk-reward appeal.

items.title: BEML shares rally 8% after Rs 590 crore defence order win
items.description: BEML Limited shares jumped after winning a ₹590 crore defence order from the Ministry of Defence. The stock has gained strong momentum, rising ~21% in a month and delivering about 200% returns over three years, reflecting sustained investor interest.

items.title: Persistent Systems shares shed over 4% after Q4 results: Here's what Nomura and other brokerages said
items.description: Persistent Systems shares fell up to 4% after Q4 results despite reporting strong earnings growth. Net profit rose nearly 34% YoY to Rs 529 crore for the March quarter, while FY26 profit climbed over 33% to Rs 1,865 crore. However, some brokerages cut estimates, weighing on sentiment and dragging the stock lower.

items.title: Nestle India shares jump 3% after strong Q4. What are Macquarie, Nomura, other brokerages saying?
items.description: Nestlé India shares rose on a strong Q4 beat, with brokerages highlighting robust volume-led growth and margins, though most maintain neutral views given premium valuations despite positive earnings momentum.

items.title: Sensex slumps over 800 points, Nifty below 24,400 despite Trump's Iran war ceasefire extension
items.description: Indian markets turned negative on Wednesday as investor caution persisted despite a ceasefire deadline extension by Donald Trump. IT stocks led the decline after weak earnings from HCL Technologies, dragging peers like Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, and Tech Mahindra lower. However, defensive names such as Hindustan Unilever and NTPC posted gains.

items.title: The IPO afterlife for unicorns: How mutual funds are doubling down on next-gen leaders
items.description: Indian mutual funds have boosted their investments in five new-age companies. Funds poured into stocks like Urban Company, Ather Energy, Lenskart, Meesho, and PhysicsWallah. This shows growing confidence from domestic investors in these tech-focused businesses. Brokerages are also initiating coverage with positive outlooks. This trend indicates a significant shift in institutional capital towards India's new-age economy.

items.title: Tata Investment shares soar over 5% after Q4 results, dividend announcement: Check details
items.description: Tata Investment shares rise over 5% after a strong Q4 performance with profit jumping ~69% YoY and a ₹3.40 dividend announcement, reflecting robust investment income and shareholder returns.

items.title: TARIL shares crash 11% after Q4 results, dividend announcement: What’s spooking investors?
items.description: Shares of Transformers and Rectifiers (India) slumped over 11% on Wednesday after Q4 results showed a dip in consolidated net profit despite strong revenue growth and a large order book. Margin pressures and rising expenses appear to have spooked investors, even as the company announced a dividend and outlined fresh capex plans.

items.title: Rs 92,000 crore ripple effect! HCL Tech’s weak Q4 drags IT pack; Infosys, Tech Mahindra slump up to 6%
items.description: HCL Technologies’s weak Q4 triggered a ₹92,000 crore sell-off in IT stocks, dragging peers like Infosys and Tech Mahindra down up to 6% amid sector-wide concerns.

items.title: Morgan Stanley reiterates ‘Overweight’ rating on TCS, sees 10% upside potential
items.description: Tata Consultancy Services is gaining attention after Morgan Stanley reiterated an “Overweight” rating with a ₹2,880 target, implying ~10% upside. Despite short-term pressure on the stock, the brokerage expects a recovery in growth and potential valuation re-rating, signalling a possible turnaround.

items.title: Tech Mahindra declares Rs 36/share final dividend; sets July 3 as record date
items.description: Tech Mahindra's board has proposed a final dividend of Rs 36 per share for FY26, bringing the total payout to Rs 51. This comes as the IT giant reported a strong March quarter with net profit up 16% year-on-year. Shareholders will vote on the dividend at the upcoming AGM, with July 3 set as the record date.

items.title: Pahalgam anniversary: How the 2025 terror attack triggered Rs 3 lakh crore defence boom and created 3 multibagger stocks
items.description: One year after the Pahalgam terror attack, India’s defence sector has entered a major upcycle, adding Rs 2.9 lakh crore in market cap as the Nifty India Defence Index gained 37%. Stocks like MTAR Technologies, Apollo Micro Systems, and Data Patterns turned multibaggers, supported by record FY26 procurement approvals worth Rs 9.3 lakh crore.

items.title: Is it worth taking a fresh look at the housing finance sector? 6 housing finance stocks with upside potential of up to 18%
items.description: Housing finance is one of those sectors where the macro picture is always attractive, but not so much the micro reality. At the level of the economy, the case is easy to make. Housing is a genuine multiplier. Every home built sets off activity across an entire chain: Cement, bricks, steel, tiles, pipes, sanitaryware, electrical fittings, paints, logistics, and labour. Few sectors transmit economic activity so widely. That is why housing finance, in principle, should be among the most durable long-term opportunities in Indian financials. But the fact is that it has produced both scams like DHFL and wealth creators like HDFC.
